summary: Light steel fire tower recorded on Yantha Mountain in Ontario's Madawaska Valley; one firelookout.ca record and a 1963 map entry, with no source on its fate.

facts.design: light steel tower with guys and an octagonal cupola

evidence.supports: Location on Yantha Mountain, Madawaska Valley, Renfrew County (record spells it 'Moutain')
evidence.quote: Yantha Moutain, Madawaska Valley, Renfrew County

evidence.supports: Light steel tower with guys, built by Goold, Shapley & Muir Co. Ltd.
evidence.quote: Light steel w. guys; built by Goold, Shapley & Muir Co. Ltd.

evidence.supports: Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, third edition, 1977
evidence.quote: Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 3rd ed., 1977.

evidence.supports: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map of 1963
Most of the towers were erected between the 1920s and the 1950s
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers came under the Department of Lands and Forests, which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: Province count by 1947: 52 wooden and 227 steel towers
evidence.quote: By 1947, there were 52 wooden and 227 steel towers across Ontario.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: One firelookout.ca record is the only tower-specific source. Its 1977 and 1963 map entries are reported as the record states them; the maps were not opened. The record spells the mountain 'Yantha Moutain' (sic); the story uses the usual spelling, and the quote keeps the record's spelling. The builder and cost come from the record and are unverified. No source gives a build year, status, height, access or current condition, so no events or visit facts are recorded. The Ontario-wide context comes from a volunteer history site and a Sudbury News feature, not from Renfrew County records. The brief's local_unit 'Renfrew County' matches the record; the brief's lat/lon (45.473611, -77.5925) were not checked against any source.
